_meta.active: COBICISTAT; ELVITEGRAVIR; EMTRICITABINE; TENOFOVIR DISOPROXIL FUMARATE
_meta.indication: STRIBILD is indicated for use as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-naive adult patients, and should not be coadministered with other antiretroviral products.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled trial of STRIBILD (E/C/F/T) versus ATRIPLA (EFV/FTC/TDF), 1:1 randomization
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-1 infected, antiretroviral treatment-naive adults with baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) above 70 mL/min
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with virologic success (HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/ml) at Week 48 using the FDA-defined snapshot analysis (non-inferiority margin 12%)
pivotal_trials.result: Virologic success 88% STRIBILD vs 84% ATRIPLA; treatment difference 3.6% (95% CI -1.6%, 8.8%), demonstrating non-inferiority

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Stribild Versus Atripla in Human Immunodeficiency Virus, Type 1 (HIV-1) Infected, Antiretroviral Treatment-Naive Adults

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled international trial of STRIBILD (E/C/F/T) versus atazanavir 300 mg + ritonavir 100 mg + TRUVADA, 1:1 randomization
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/ml at Week 48
pivotal_trials.result: Virologic success 90% STRIBILD vs 87% ATV/r + TRUVADA; treatment difference 3.0% (95% CI -1.9%, 7.8%), demonstrating non-inferiority

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Stribild Versus Ritonavir-Boosted Atazanavir Plus Truvada in Human Immunodeficiency Virus, Type 1 (HIV-1) Infected, Antiretroviral Treatment-Naive Adults

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) were nausea (16%) and diarrhea (12%). Safety based on 1408 subjects. Key identified risks include new onset/worsening renal impairment and proximal renal tubulopathy (the cobicistat component has been shown to increase serum creatinine due to inhibition of tubular secretion of creatinine without affecting renal glomerular function; elevation in serum creatinine occurred in 7% of STRIBILD subjects vs 1% ATRIPLA and 4% ATV/r+TRUVADA) and decreases in bone mineral density.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination: elvitegravir is an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor; emtricitabine and tenofovir DF are nucleoside/nucleotide analogues that inhibit HIV-1 reverse transcriptase; cobicistat is a mechanism-based CYP3A inhibitor that pharmacokinetically boosts elvitegravir.
modality: Small molecule fixed-dose combination tablet (elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, tenofovir DF)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS/SEVERE HEPATOMEGALY WITH STEATOSIS and POST TREATMENT ACUTE EXACERBATION OF HEPATITIS B. Lactic acidosis and severe hepatomegaly with steatosis, including fatal cases, have been reported with nucleoside analogs including tenofovir DF; severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in HBV/HIV-1 coinfected patients who discontinued products containing emtricitabine or tenofovir DF.

advisory_committee.vote: The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee met May 11, 2012 and voted 13 YES to 1 NO on the question of whether, considering the overall risks and benefits, the available data support approval of E/C/F/T as a complete regimen for treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-naive adults.

summary.text: NDA 203100 for the STRIBILD (E/C/F/T) fixed-dose combination was submitted/received October 27, 2011 and reviewed under standard review with a PDUFA goal date of August 27, 2012. The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee met May 11, 2012 and voted 13-1 that the data support approval. Approval was based on two Phase 3 non-inferiority trials (GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103) demonstrating virologic success at Week 48 (traditional approval, not accelerated); the application was approved first cycle on August 27, 2012 with multiple postmarketing requirements and no REMS.

The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee met on May 11, 2012, to discuss new drug application (NDA) 203100, for a fixed-dose combination tablet of EVG/COBI/FTC/TDF, submitted by Gilead Sciences, Inc.

The FDA Guidance, "Antiretroviral Drugs Using Plasma HIV RNA Measurements-Clinical Considerations for Accelerated and Traditional Approval" states that 48-Week data can be used for traditional approval.
There are no recommendations for Postmarket Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies related to this NDA submission.

requirement.text: 1919-2: Conduct a pediatric PK, safety, and antiviral activity trial of Stribild in subjects 6 to <12 years of age over at least 48 weeks, including renal and bone (DEXA) safety monitoring.

citations.quote: monitoring over at least 48 weeks of dosing in pediatric subjects from 6 to < 12 years of age. Dose selection must be based on pharmacokinetic data for component drugs and must be discussed with FDA prior to initiation of trial. Include in the trial safety monitoring assessment of potential renal toxicity (serial assessments of serum creatinine, serum phosphate, urine glucose, urine protein, calculated creatinine clearance, glomerular filtration rate (GFR) by cystatin C, and calculated fractional excretion of phosphate) and effects on bone (to include serial DEXA assessment).

requirement.text: 1919-7: Perform a clinical trial (approximately 500 women) to characterize incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women, with a renal monitoring algorithm similar to that used in GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103.

citations.quote: 1919-7 Perform a clinical trial to better characterize the incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women. Provide adequate renal monitoring in the proposed trial to assess renal safety employing a renal monitoring algorithm similar to that used in GS-US-236-0102 and GS-US-236-0103. The algorithm will include an assessment of serum creatinine, creatinine clearance by Cockcroft-Gault, glomerular filtration rate (GFR) by cystatin C, serum phosphate, renal phosphate threshold (TmP/GFR), urine protein and urine glucose. The trial will enroll approximately 500 women, in order to assess the relative incidence of and risk factors for renal adverse events in women as compared to men enrolled in other Stribild clinical trials.
